1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioner mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its LAC no. 125 /
2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Roop Chand v. Union of India Page no. 2 of 12 specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3.

sentences.text:
The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas Sh. Roop Chand vs Union Of India on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157784038/
1 land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees,
tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioner is the cobhumidar and is in possession of his share in land bearing Khasra no. 47/3 (416), 47/8 (316) total admeasuring 8 bighas and 12 biswas (in short, the said land) as per the revenue record situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi.
5. It is stated that the petitioner is entitled to receive the compensation amount of the actual prevailing market value of the said land.
LAC no. 125 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Roop Chand v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12

sentences.text:
The ld. LAC has failed in assessing the price of the said land and the said award has been passed amount of which is inadequate, arbitrary, unjust, illusionary, without any reasonable aspects, and the award is not acceptable to the petitioner.
6. It is submitted that the said award has been passed with grave error and the ld. LAC has failed to appreciate the law points involved.

The ld. LAC in assessment of market value of the said land has been guided by the notions and assumptions, rather the reality of the facts points towards a steady rise in the value of the said land owing to largescale purchase of land by private builders, business houses, industrialists on a very cumulative rates during the past several years, therefore, the market value of the said land is higher than the value assessed by the ld. LAC 7.

The ld. LAC has ignored the facts that the said land is surrounded with the land of much higher rates and he has also ignored the facts that the said land was the only source of income of the petitioner, and after acquisition of the said land, the petitioner has become unemployed.
The ld.

LAC has also ignored the fact that the said land is very fertile and having good potential, and commercial crops were sown by the petitioner, and the said land was the only source of income of the petitioner.

The principles for assessment of the market value of land in village Rani Khera and nearby villages/residential areas are not taken into consideration, and prices of land in the vicinity of the said land are much higher than that of the said land, at LAC no. 125 / 2016 (Award No.
08/200506/DC(NW)) Roop Chand v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 12 the time of acquisition of the said land.

entities.text: Roop Chand v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The assessment of the market value of the said land has been done arbitrarily by ignoring the principle of natural justice, and if necessary inquiry had been conducted, the market value of the said land would have not been less than Rs. 10,000/ per square yards.

8. It is submitted that the ld. LAC has totally ignored the facts that the said land is adjacent to the main road which is having well developed farmhouses, main roads and even the railway line is also passing in the vicinity of the said land.
The said land is also very fertile land having great potentiality and substantial value.
The learned LAC has also ignored the facts that all the basic facilities like Sh. Roop Chand vs Union Of India on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157784038/

sentences.text: 2 electricity, water, telephone, banks, post offices, schools, hospital, food supplies office, roads are available in the village Rani Khera.

The ld. LAC has ignored the fact that the said land has great potential and situational value in as much as, on the other side of the land there is a residential colonies, which also increases the market value of the said land, and the said land now cannot be termed as agriculture land, however, ld. LAC has failed to appreciate the said fact.

It is submitted that by way of the present petition, the petitioner has sought the increase in market value of the said land @ Rs. 10,000 per square yards and the solatium @ 30% along with other additional amount along with interest from the date of notification.
LAC no. 125 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Roop Chand v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 12 9.

sentences.text:
Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/Union of India and, it has been pleaded that the said land has been acquired as disclosed in this petition and, it is, inter alia,
submitted that the petitioner is not entitled for compensation in respect of construction of structure,
which is placed without the sanction of law, and in terms of section 4 notification there were no structure, tree, well on the said land.
The said land is not surrounded by any developed or undeveloped colony and can be used for agricultural purposes only.
The ld. LAC categorised the land into three categories on the basis of survey carried out as per the fertility and user of land.
The plain agricultural land of standard quality was included in "Block A".
The land consisting of gaddah upto 23 feet from which soil has been lifted was included in "Block B" and the land consisting of gaddah upto 46 feet was included in category of "Block C".
The ld. LAC considered value of land as detailed in the sale deeds registered in the office of SubRegistrar in proximity to the notification.

The ld.
LAC has considered the sale transaction of similar land situated in the vicinity, and the small pieces of land in square yards cannot be compared with the huge land covered under the acquisition

,
therefore, the registered sale deed could not be relied upon in order to assess the fair market value of the land.

10. It is submitted that the ld. LAC has assessed the fair market value of the said land by adopting the indicative price fixed by the government of NCT of Delhi @ Rs. 15,70,000 per acre for the year 2001  2002 which is LAC no. 125 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Roop Chand v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 12 applicable with effect from 01.04.2001.

entities.text: Roop Chand v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The ld. LAC adopted the indicative price fixed by the Government of NCT of Delhi of land falling in "Block B".

As far as the land having ghadda upto 23 feet, the ld. LAC has deducted Rs. 1,70,000 per acre from the market value of "Block B"
category land, therefore, after deduction the value comes to Rs. 14,00,000 per acre,
and as such the market value of the said land was assessed as per the rate prevailing during the corresponding period for different categories of land besides other statutory benefits.
It is submitted that the ld. LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view the aspects enumerated under Section 23 and 24 of the Act.
All the other averments made in the petition was denied in toto and it has been submitted that the reference filed by the petitioner is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: 12. Written statement has been filed on behalf of the respondent no.3/DSIDC, and, inter alia, it is submitted that the claim filed by the petitioner is time barred and has been filed on the false and fictitious grounds, therefore, the present petition is liable to be dismissed.
The present petition is also not maintainable as the said land is governed by the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954.

13. It is submitted that as per Kabza kariwahi report dated 29.11.2007, the said land has been acquired/handed over at the instance of DSIIDC and it has no concern whatsoever with regard to the fixation of compensation, as all the aspects have already been dealt it by the ld. LAC.
The area of the said land has been admitted only to the extent as specified by the ld. LAC in his statement under Section 19 of the Act.
The petitioner has not led any evidence in respect of the relief claimed.
The said land was also not surrounded by the any developed or under developed colonies and was being used for only agriculture purposes.
There were no standing trees, boundary walls etc. on the said land at the time of acquisition.
All the other contents of the petition are denied in toto.
It is prayed that the reference petition filed by the petitioners is liable to be dismissed with cost.

sentences.text: I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  LAC no. 125 / 2016 (Award No.
08/200506/DC(NW)) Roop Chand v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 12 WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT ? OPP 18.

entities.text: Roop Chand v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioner to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
19.

entities.text: State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To prove their case, the petitioner, through his counsel has adopted the evidence led in case Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioner in the aforementioned case.
20. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

21. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

In LAC no. 125 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Roop Chand v. Union of India Page no. 10 of 12 view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.

entities.text: Roop Chand v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 22. In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioner herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
The petitioner is accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioner as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
23. The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioner shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.

Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
